textbookText: Cathode (-) : A thin strip of pure copper Electrolyte: Acidified copper sulfate (CuS𝑂4) solution. Procedure: 1. Immerse the anode and cathode into the beaker containing the electrolyte. 2. Connect the electrodes to a DC battery (Anode to positive terminal, Cathode to negative). 3. Pass an electric current through the solution for 15–20 minutes. Observations: The Anode (impure) gradually becomes thinner as it dissolves. The Cathode (pure) becomes thicker as pure metal deposits on it. Insoluble impurities collect below the anode as Anode Mud. Chemical Reactions: At Anode (Oxidation): Cu → 𝐶𝑢++ + 2𝑒− At Cathode (Reduction): 𝐶𝑢++ + 2𝑒− → Cu Conclusion: By passing electricity, metal ions move from the impure anode into the solution and then deposit as 99.9% pure metal onto the cathode. ***
